feed.subtitle: Research papers and global crypto regulation, at a glance
feed.rights: Explanations and summaries are generated by AI from the original text. Dates, rates and amounts are checked against the source, but errors are still possible, so always rely on the original. Nothing here is legal, tax or investment advice.

entry.title: Legal challenge to FCA motor finance compensation scheme to be heard in February 2027
entry.summary: Motor finance legal challenge to be heard in February 2027 FCA · Oct 13, 2026 The Upper Tribunal will hear legal challenges to the FCA's motor finance compensation scheme from 16 to 26 February 2027. The scheme is currently partially suspended, but firms must keep preparing and progressing complaints. The document also gives advice to lenders and consumers, including that consumers can complain directly to their lender for free and need not use a law firm or claims management company.

entry.title: Bullseye Financial Ltd enters administration
entry.summary: Bullseye Financial Ltd enters administration FCA · Oct 27, 2026 Bullseye Financial Ltd entered administration on 23 October 2026, with Robert Young of Azets Holdings Limited and Matthew Haw of RSM UK Restructuring Advisory LLP appointed as joint administrators. The FCA-authorised firm served only professional investors and agreed on 11 March 2026 to stop carrying out any regulated activity. The notice provides contact details for customers and warns about fraudsters posing as the firm or its administrators.

entry.title: Financial planning firm IMFP and its representative IMA enter administration
entry.summary: InterestMe Financial Planning Limited (IMFP) and the appointed representative InterestMe Advisers Limited (IMA) enter administration FCA · Sep 28, 2026 The FCA reports that IMFP and its appointed representative IMA entered administration on 24 September 2026, with Kroll Advisory Limited's two joint administrators taking control. The notice explains how customers can contact the administrators, what to do about investments and complaints, and warns about fraudsters impersonating the firms or administrators.

entry.title: FCA secures bankruptcy order against Arthur Temlett
entry.summary: FCA secures bankruptcy order against Arthur Temlett FCA · Sep 28, 2026 The FCA asked the court to make Arthur Temlett, trading as Abacus Insurance Consultants, bankrupt, known as sequestration in Scotland. The Sheriff granted the application on 27 August 2026, and Emma Porter of Aver Chartered Accountants was appointed trustee to assess his finances and distribute any recovered funds to creditors. Mr Temlett is awaiting trial on embezzlement charges following a Police Scotland investigation.

entry.title: UK regulator secures repayment for crypto fraud victims
entry.summary: FCA secures money back for victims of crypto fraud FCA · Sep 28, 2026 · Crypto The FCA obtained confiscation orders against Raymondip Bedi and Patrick Mavanga, who ran a fake cryptoasset investment scheme that defrauded at least 65 investors of £1,541,799. On 28 September 2026, Bedi was ordered to pay £603,404.28 and Mavanga £247,997.99. The FCA says funds recovered through the process will be returned to victims.

entry.title: FCA Survey: Firms' Satisfaction, Confidence and Trust in the Regulator Rise
entry.summary: Firms’ confidence, satisfaction and trust in the FCA rise FCA · Oct 2, 2026 The FCA and Practitioner Panel's 2026 annual survey of regulated firms found that 79% are highly satisfied with their relationship with the FCA, up from 74%. Firms also rated the FCA as highly effective more often, and 88% said they understand what the FCA expects under the Consumer Duty. Firms still want progress on regulatory burden, and the FCA says it is simplifying data requests.

entry.title: FCA appoints new Board members including two non-executive directors and deputy chief executive
entry.summary: FCA announces new Board appointments FCA · Sep 30, 2026 The UK Financial Conduct Authority has appointed Lea Paterson CBE and Matthew Tobin as non-executive directors, with the Treasury making the appointments. Deputy chief executive Sarah Pritchard has also joined the Board as an executive member. The new Board roles take effect on 1 October 2026.

entry.title: FCA opens applications for regulated crypto firms in the UK
entry.summary: FCA opens the gateway to regulated crypto FCA · Sep 30, 2026 · Crypto From today, crypto firms can apply to the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) for authorisation. Crypto firms operating in the UK will be brought under full FCA regulation, with standards covering consumer protection, safeguarding, market integrity and financial resilience. Firms intending to keep operating must apply by 28 February 2027, and the new regime comes into force on 25 October 2027.

entry.title: Two people plead guilty to fraud that cost four clients £2m
entry.summary: Two plead guilty after clients lose £2m in fraud case FCA · Oct 13, 2026 Two staff at financial advice firms pleaded guilty at Portsmouth Crown Court to charges brought by the FCA. They admitted defrauding clients between January 2019 and January 2023 and using false documents, causing four clients to lose £2m. One has also admitted a money laundering offence. Sentencing is set for 10 December 2026, and the FCA will seek confiscation of criminal benefit.

entry.title: UK capital market reform to serve the economy better (FCA speech)
entry.summary: Reforming UK capital markets to ensure they work well for our economy FCA · Oct 5, 2026 · Crypto Jon Relleen, FCA director of infrastructure and exchanges, delivered this speech at a 5 October 2026 summit on reforming UK capital market rules. He says the FCA has completed major parts of a multi-year programme aimed at supporting growth while preserving trust, market integrity and high standards. The speech cites delivered changes such as the revamped listing regime, the new public offers framework and improved bond and derivatives transparency.

entry.title: FCA reviews how it engages with whistleblowers
entry.summary: Looking at how we interact with whistleblowers FCA · Oct 6, 2026 The UK Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) mourns the death of a whistleblower it had long been in contact with and outlines how it works with whistleblowers. Of the 1,252 whistleblowing reports closed last year, 42% led to direct action to manage or reduce harm, and 53% informed wider work and harm prevention. The FCA has asked new independent non-executive director Lea Paterson to review its interactions with this whistleblower and plans to share lessons early next year.

entry.title: UK FCA proposes notice periods for long-term investment fund redemptions
entry.summary: New rules to make long-term investment funds clearer FCA · Oct 8, 2026 The FCA has set out clearer expectations for asset managers investing in long-term assets such as property. Under the proposed rules, investors would need to give 90 days' notice to access their funds. Existing funds would have 2 years to comply and must give investors at least 1 year's notice. Feedback on the proposals is requested by 11 December 2026.

entry.title: Strong compliance functions help keep corporate finance markets trusted
entry.summary: Strong compliance functions support trusted corporate finance markets FCA · Oct 8, 2026 · Crypto The UK FCA reports findings from a survey of 411 corporate finance firms on their compliance functions, receiving 382 responses. Most firms carry out key compliance activities, but gaps remain in areas such as whistleblowing arrangements, breach registers and performance assessment. The FCA asks firms to reflect on their arrangements and says it will engage further with selected firms.

entry.title: Liam Coleman appointed chair of the Financial Ombudsman Service, which resolves financial complaints
entry.summary: Liam Coleman appointed as chair of the Financial Ombudsman Service FCA · Oct 9, 2026 The FCA Board has appointed Liam Coleman as permanent chair of the Financial Ombudsman Service, with Treasury approval. He takes up the role on 10 October 2026 for a 3-year term, having served as interim chair for the past year. The service resolves complaints between financial businesses and their customers.

entry.title: Building the future of finance in the age of AI
entry.summary: Building the future of finance in the age of AI FCA · Oct 19, 2026 A drafted speech by FCA chief data, information and intelligence officer Jessica Rusu at Bloomberg's UK Policy Series, which may differ from the delivered version. It sets out the FCA's approach to the safe and responsible adoption of AI in financial services, including its response to the Mills Review. It also covers clearer disclaimers for consumers and examples of good and poor AI practice.

entry.title: Economic Secretary's UK Digital Assets Week speech on digitising financial markets
entry.summary: Economic Secretary to the Treasury speech for UK Digital Assets Week HMRC / gov.uk · Oct 6, 2026 · Crypto The Economic Secretary to the Treasury gave a speech at UK Digital Assets Week setting out the government's ambition to lead globally in digital assets. The speech cites the Wholesale Financial Markets Digital Strategy, the appointment of a Wholesale Digital Markets Champion, and approvals for HSBC and ClearToken to operate Digital Securities Depositories in the Digital Securities Sandbox. It also outlines a pilot issuance of the Digital Gilt Instrument (DIGIT) planned for the first quarter of 2027.

entry.title: FCA arrests three in major operation against insider dealing crime ring
entry.summary: Three arrests in major FCA operation against criminal insider dealing ring FCA · Oct 13, 2026 The FCA and the National Crime Agency jointly searched five residential premises in London and Manchester and arrested three individuals. The operation targets a suspected organised criminal group involved in insider dealing and money laundering. More than 30 devices were seized, and the suspects are being interviewed by the FCA.

entry.title: Jarvis Investment Management Limited enters special administration
entry.summary: Jarvis Investment Management Limited enters special administration FCA · Oct 15, 2026 On 14 October 2026, Jarvis Investment Management Limited entered special administration, with Adam Stephens and Philip Hemming of S&W Partners LLP appointed as special administrators. The firm remains FCA authorised and regulated, and the administrators will assess client money and custody assets and work to return them to clients. Clients are advised to contact their financial adviser first and to remain alert to scams.

entry.title: ePayments Systems Limited enters special administration, with two joint administrators appointed.
entry.summary: ePayments Systems Limited enters special administration FCA · Oct 15, 2026 On 15 October 2026, e-money firm ePayments Systems Limited (EPS) entered special administration, with Mark Boast and Allister Manson of Opus Restructuring LLP appointed as joint special administrators. The special administrators will assess all funds held by the firm and gather information from creditors and customers. EPS remains FCA authorised and subject to FCA rules, and customers can contact the FCA Consumer Helpline for more information.

entry.title: Revocation of bans related to LIBOR/EURIBOR
entry.summary: LIBOR/EURIBOR-related bans FCA · Oct 16, 2026 The FCA reviewed its regulatory action against individuals whose convictions were recently overturned by the Court of Appeal. Because those convictions were the basis for its action, the FCA has revoked the bans on Colin Bermingham, Philippe Moryoussef, Jonathan Mathew and Christian Bittar and removed the related Final Notices from its channels. It will take no further action against these individuals on this matter.

entry.title: Former CEO banned after acting as front for disqualified director in £4m high-risk bond losses
entry.summary: Former chief executive banned after misconduct led to £4m losses in high-risk investments FCA · Oct 21, 2026 The FCA has banned Jeffrey Dawkins, former chief executive of Vector Wealth Ltd, and fined him nearly £270,000. He acted as a front for a disqualified director, letting that person use the firm's FCA authorisation to sell high-risk mini-bonds. Investors are expected to lose about £4 million.

entry.title: Speech on deliberately reshaping regulation by the FCA's deputy chief executive
entry.summary: Reshaping regulation, deliberately FCA · Oct 21, 2026 · Crypto Sarah Pritchard, deputy chief executive of the UK Financial Conduct Authority, gave this speech at the Investment Association Annual Dinner on 20 October 2026. She says the FCA is past the peak of rule making but continues a strategic approach to reform. She encourages firms to engage and identify where friction lies.

entry.title: UK financial regulator FCA signs deal for new Leeds office
entry.summary: Leeds office move FCA · Oct 22, 2026 The FCA has signed an agreement for a new 36,097 sq ft office at 2 Wellington Place, Leeds, to become its long-term base from 2028. Its current Leeds office at 6 Queen Street has grown since opening in 2022. The move supports the FCA's five-year strategy goal of having 1,000 roles outside London by 2030. More details will be shared closer to 2028.

entry.title: Market integrity in a digital age: FCA chief executive's City Dinner speech
entry.summary: Market integrity in a digital age FCA · Oct 22, 2026 · Crypto Nikhil Rathi, chief executive of the UK Financial Conduct Authority (FCA), delivered this speech at the City of London Corporation's annual City Dinner at Mansion House. He argues that fast technological change brings opportunities but also serious threats to market integrity, including market abuse and financial crime, and that the regulatory system responds too slowly. He says the FCA will make better use of technology and intelligence and use its powers more assertively, and stresses that stronger partnerships between regulators, industry and government are essential.

entry.title: UK FCA restricts six unregulated lenders over anti-money laundering control concerns
entry.summary: FCA restricts 6 firms following concerns over anti-money laundering controls FCA · Oct 23, 2026 · Crypto The FCA has placed voluntary restrictions on six Annex 1 firms, unregulated lenders, after raising concerns about their anti-money laundering policies, controls and procedures. The restrictions limit their ability to take on new customers or do new business with existing customers, including extending credit. The FCA is also assessing responses to an information request sent to around 900 registered Annex 1 firms.

entry.title: Beyond borders: FCA Chair Ashley Alder's speech on regulating shared risks
entry.summary: Beyond borders: Regulating the risks we share FCA · Oct 23, 2026 FCA Chair Ashley Alder delivered this speech at the Michael D. Gill Lecture on 13 October 2026. He argues that risks travel across firms, sectors, supply chains and jurisdictions, so regulation must address shared dependencies that can transmit shocks through the financial system. He also states that growth and resilience are not opposing goals, and that regulators need to share intelligence, test cross-border scenarios and prepare to act together.

entry.title: FCA urges private market firms to manage conflicts of interest as the sector grows
entry.summary: FCA calls on private market firms to manage conflicts of interest in line with rapid growth FCA · Oct 23, 2026 An FCA review found that private market firms vary in how well they identify and manage conflicts of interest. Covering private equity, private credit and real estate, it noted good practice but also recurring weaknesses in cross-fund transfers, multi-party transactions, gifts and entertainment, and information barriers. The FCA expects firms to identify, record, manage and disclose conflicts effectively and show that investors are treated fairly.

entry.title: Chandler King (City) Limited Enters Creditors' Voluntary Liquidation
entry.summary: Chandler King (City) Limited enters creditors’ voluntary liquidation FCA · Oct 26, 2026 Chandler King (City) Limited was an FCA-authorised independent financial adviser covering investments and pensions. It entered creditors' voluntary liquidation on 17 September 2026, with Grace Jones and Karyn Jones of Parker Andrews appointed as joint liquidators. The liquidators will assess client money and custody assets and work with the Financial Services Compensation Scheme (FSCS), which covers eligible clients up to £85,000.

entry.title: UK regulator examines whether defence SMEs can access banking services
entry.summary: Defence SMEs need banking services that work FCA · Oct 26, 2026 The FCA examined whether small and medium-sized defence businesses can access banking services efficiently and consistently. It found the main issue is friction and delay, such as long onboarding and repeated information requests, rather than widespread exclusion. The FCA says firms should take proportionate, risk-based decisions and that defence should not be treated as a single category.

entry.title: Self Assessment deadline in 100 days: filing your 2025–26 tax return
entry.summary: Self Assessment deadline incoming – 100 days to go HMRC / gov.uk · Oct 23, 2026 · Crypto HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) urges Self Assessment customers to file their 2025 to 2026 tax return early, with the deadline set for 31 January 2027. Filing early on GOV.UK lets people learn how much tax they owe, budget in advance, get refunds sooner and avoid penalties. The notice also lists available guidance, support tools and warnings about HMRC impersonation scams.
